title: Deep Squat: Overview
text: Exercise: Deep Squat. Category: lower_limb_rehabilitation. Purpose: Represent a squat movement for posture and consistency analysis; Support explanations of alignment and controlled descent; Provide research-grounded movement descriptors. Starting position: Stand using the stance specified by the care team; Keep the feet stable on the floor; Begin with an upright, controlled trunk position.

title: Deep Squat: Movement phases
text: descent: The hips and knees flex as the body moves downward.; bottom_position: The lowest configured position is reached while alignment is maintained.; ascent: The hips and knees extend as the body returns to standing.

title: Deep Squat: General guidance
text: Use only the depth assigned by the care team.; Keep the feet stable and the knees aligned with the feet.; Keep the trunk controlled.; Move down and up smoothly.

title: Deep Squat: Safety limits
text: This record does not define a safe squat depth for a specific patient.; Use assistance or supervision when required.; Stop for severe pain, sudden weakness, dizziness, or loss of balance.

title: Deep Squat: knee_valgus_or_misalignment
text: Possible execution issue: knee_valgus_or_misalignment. Observable signals: knees moving inward; knees not aligned over feet. Safe explanation: The knees may not have remained aligned with the feet.

title: Deep Squat: excessive_trunk_flexion
text: Possible execution issue: excessive_trunk_flexion. Observable signals: large forward trunk angle. Safe explanation: The trunk may have leaned forward more than expected.

title: Deep Squat: limited_depth
text: Possible execution issue: limited_depth. Observable signals: reduced knee or hip flexion relative to configured target. Safe explanation: The movement may not have reached the configured target depth.

title: Deep Squat: heel_lift
text: Possible execution issue: heel_lift. Observable signals: loss of heel contact; pressure shift toward forefoot. Safe explanation: The heels may not have remained in stable contact with the floor.

title: Hurdle Step: Overview
text: Exercise: Hurdle Step. Category: lower_limb_rehabilitation. Purpose: Represent a stepping movement involving single-leg support; Support balance and lower-limb alignment analysis. Starting position: Stand in the setup specified by the care team; Use support when required; Maintain a stable trunk before stepping.

title: Hurdle Step: Movement phases
text: weight_shift: Body weight shifts onto the supporting leg.; step_over: The moving leg lifts and passes over the obstacle.; placement: The foot is placed while balance is maintained.; return: The user returns to the starting position with control.

title: Hurdle Step: General guidance
text: Use support when assigned.; Move slowly and keep the supporting leg stable.; Lift the stepping foot only as high as required.; Return to the starting position with control.

title: Hurdle Step: Safety limits
text: The obstacle height and support requirements must come from the care plan.; This exercise may create a fall risk and should not be attempted without required supervision.; Stop after a near-fall, fall, severe pain, or sudden weakness.

title: Hurdle Step: support_leg_misalignment
text: Possible execution issue: support_leg_misalignment. Observable signals: hip, knee, or ankle moving out of vertical alignment. Safe explanation: The supporting leg may not have remained aligned during the step.

title: Hurdle Step: trunk_sway
text: Possible execution issue: trunk_sway. Observable signals: large lateral trunk movement. Safe explanation: The trunk may have moved sideways to compensate for balance.

title: Hurdle Step: insufficient_clearance
text: Possible execution issue: insufficient_clearance. Observable signals: low foot clearance relative to obstacle. Safe explanation: The moving foot may not have cleared the obstacle by the configured margin.

title: Hurdle Step: loss_of_balance
text: Possible execution issue: loss_of_balance. Observable signals: rapid corrective movements; unexpected foot placement. Safe explanation: The movement may have required an unexpected balance correction.

title: Seated Knee Extension: Overview
text: Exercise: Seated Knee Extension. Category: lower_limb_rehabilitation. Purpose: Represent controlled knee-extension movement for dashboard explanations; Support repetition and posture analysis; Describe observable movement phases without prescribing treatment. Starting position: Sit in a stable chair with the back supported when appropriate; Keep the thigh supported and the trunk steady; Begin with the knee flexed and the foot in a comfortable resting position; Follow the range and duration configured by the care team.

title: Seated Knee Extension: Movement phases
text: rest: The leg remains near the starting position before movement begins.; lift: The lower leg moves forward and upward as the knee extends.; hold: The target position is maintained for the configured duration, when a hold is part of the care plan.; lower: The lower leg returns gradually to the starting position.

title: Seated Knee Extension: General guidance
text: Sit upright and keep the thigh steady.; Raise the lower leg smoothly.; Use only the range and hold time assigned by the care team.; Lower the leg slowly and with control.

title: Seated Knee Extension: Safety limits
text: This guide is educational and does not prescribe a patient-specific range of motion.; Stop and seek appropriate help for severe pain, sudden weakness, dizziness, a fall, or loss of balance.; Target angles, repetitions, resistance, and hold times must come from the care plan or clinician.

title: Seated Knee Extension: insufficient_extension
text: Possible execution issue: insufficient_extension. Observable signals: reduced knee angle; reduced shin lift angle. Safe explanation: The lower leg may not have reached the configured target position.

title: Seated Knee Extension: movement_too_fast_or_abrupt
text: Possible execution issue: movement_too_fast_or_abrupt. Observable signals: high angular velocity; short lift duration; high jerk score. Safe explanation: The movement may have been performed faster or less smoothly than expected.

title: Seated Knee Extension: short_hold
text: Possible execution issue: short_hold. Observable signals: hold duration below configured target. Safe explanation: The raised position was not maintained for the configured duration.

title: Seated Knee Extension: trunk_or_hip_compensation
text: Possible execution issue: trunk_or_hip_compensation. Observable signals: increased trunk lean; thigh movement; hip lift from chair. Safe explanation: The upper body or thigh may have moved to compensate during the exercise.

title: Side Lunge: Overview
text: Exercise: Side Lunge. Category: lower_limb_rehabilitation. Purpose: Represent controlled lateral stepping and lowering; Support alignment, symmetry, and balance analysis. Starting position: Stand using the stance specified by the care team; Keep the trunk controlled; Use support when required.

title: Side Lunge: Movement phases
text: lateral_step: One foot steps to the side.; lower: The body lowers toward the stepping side as the hip and knee flex.; push_return: The user pushes through the stepping leg and returns to the starting position.

title: Side Lunge: General guidance
text: Use only the step width and depth assigned by the care team.; Keep the knee aligned with the foot.; Keep the trunk controlled.; Return to the starting position smoothly.

title: Side Lunge: Safety limits
text: Use required support or supervision.; The chatbot must not prescribe step width, depth, or repetition count.; Stop for severe pain, sudden weakness, dizziness, or loss of balance.

title: Side Lunge: knee_misalignment
text: Possible execution issue: knee_misalignment. Observable signals: knee moving inward or away from foot alignment. Safe explanation: The knee may not have remained aligned with the foot.

title: Side Lunge: excessive_trunk_lean
text: Possible execution issue: excessive_trunk_lean. Observable signals: large lateral or forward trunk angle. Safe explanation: The trunk may have leaned more than expected during the movement.

title: Side Lunge: limited_lateral_control
text: Possible execution issue: limited_lateral_control. Observable signals: abrupt step; high jerk score; unstable return. Safe explanation: The side step or return may have been less controlled than expected.

title: Sit to Stand: Overview
text: Exercise: Sit to Stand. Category: lower_limb_rehabilitation. Purpose: Represent the transition between sitting and standing; Support posture, balance, and repetition analysis; Describe observable movement features for chatbot explanations. Starting position: Sit on a stable chair using the setup specified by the care team; Place the feet in a stable position; Keep the trunk controlled before initiating the movement.

title: Sit to Stand: Movement phases
text: preparation: The user prepares to rise while maintaining a stable seated position.; forward_transfer: The trunk moves forward to shift body weight over the feet.; rise: The hips and knees extend as the body rises from the chair.; standing: The user reaches a stable upright position.; descent: The hips and knees flex as the user returns to the chair with control.

title: Sit to Stand: General guidance
text: Use the chair and foot placement assigned by the care team.; Shift forward in a controlled way before standing.; Keep the knees aligned with the feet.; Return to the chair slowly and with control.

title: Sit to Stand: Safety limits
text: Use support or supervision when required by the care plan.; Do not perform the exercise if the environment is unstable or unsafe.; Stop and seek help after a fall, severe pain, sudden weakness, dizziness, or loss of balance.

title: Sit to Stand: knee_misalignment
text: Possible execution issue: knee_misalignment. Observable signals: knees moving inward or outward relative to feet. Safe explanation: The knees may not have remained aligned with the feet during the movement.

title: Sit to Stand: excessive_trunk_compensation
text: Possible execution issue: excessive_trunk_compensation. Observable signals: large trunk lean; rapid trunk motion. Safe explanation: The upper body may have moved more than expected to assist the transition.

title: Sit to Stand: asymmetric_weight_transfer
text: Possible execution issue: asymmetric_weight_transfer. Observable signals: uneven left-right pressure; uneven joint motion. Safe explanation: More weight may have been placed on one side than the other.

title: Sit to Stand: uncontrolled_descent
text: Possible execution issue: uncontrolled_descent. Observable signals: high descent velocity; high jerk score; short descent duration. Safe explanation: The return to the chair may have been faster or less controlled than expected.

title: Movement Smoothness Indicator
text: display name: Movement Smoothness Indicator. unit: implementation_defined. description: A derived measure related to abrupt changes in acceleration or movement.. patient explanation: A larger value may mean the movement was less smooth, depending on system calibration.. threshold source: system_calibration_required

title: Movement Symmetry
text: display name: Movement Symmetry. unit: implementation_defined. description: A system-specific comparison of left-side and right-side movement behavior.. patient explanation: This compares movement between the two sides.. threshold source: system_calibration_required

title: Trunk Lean

title: Inertial Measurement Unit
text: display name: Inertial Measurement Unit. measures: linear acceleration; angular velocity. components: accelerometer; gyroscope. description: A wearable sensor used to estimate motion and orientation changes.. limitations: sensor drift; placement sensitivity; calibration dependency

title: Force-Sensing Resistor
text: display name: Force-Sensing Resistor. measures: relative pressure or force. description: A pressure-sensitive element that changes electrical resistance when force is applied.. limitations: nonlinear response; placement sensitivity; requires calibration

title: Time-of-Flight Distance Sensor
text: display name: Time-of-Flight Distance Sensor. measures: distance. description: A sensor that estimates distance using the travel time of emitted light.. limitations: out-of-range readings; surface reflectivity; field-of-view effects

title: Camera Pose Estimation
text: display name: Camera Pose Estimation. measures: joint keypoint coordinates; derived joint angles. description: A computer-vision method that estimates body joint locations from images or video.. limitations: occlusion; camera angle; lighting; keypoint confidence

title: Optical Motion Capture
text: display name: Optical Motion Capture. measures: marker positions; joint kinematics. description: A laboratory system that tracks markers to estimate body motion.. limitations: laboratory setup; marker placement; occlusion; cost
